newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX treads water in dull early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German DAX treads water in dull early bourse trade.

text.p: German shares registered a generally mixed performance in early bourse dealings, but firm Bunds, strong futures and an upbeat overnight close on Wall Street looked set to boost the DAX index over the session.
Many market players extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend, which lowered volumes appreciably.
The DAX index, which measures bourse trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, was up 5.96 points, or 0.17 percent, at 3,557.92 points in early trade.
"There are positive factors coming from many sides on the German share market at the moment," Bayerische Vereinsbank said in a research document.
Despite receiving a licking in recent days by the yen and other currencies, the dollar was still seen as having a positive impact on the German share market in the mid-term.
The currency was stable early on Friday at around 1.70 marks and Vereinsbank said a rise to 1.75 marks was possible, while the strength of sterling was also helpful.
"These currency trends, combined with the appealing levels of economic growth abroad, should help improve the outlook for the export sector," said Vereinsbank.
"The clear abatement of volumes in recent days is a cause for concern," analysts at Commerzbank said.
There were some possible clouds on the horizon. "Given an eight-percent rise in the market since the start of April, a bout of profit taking cannot be ruled out," Commerzbank said.

Among the best performers in early bourse trade was Lufthansa AG, which was up 80 pfennigs, around three percent, at 27.65 marks, still riding a wave of positive sentiment following its upbeat first-quarter 1997 figures on Wednesday.
Shares in electronics giant Siemens AG hit 100 marks for the first time ever, a rise of 1.75 marks or 1.78 percent.
